---

This plan covers the whole project — the underground shelter, the entry structures,
the sentry post including its **brick masonry walls**, the services, the external
works, and testing and commissioning.

It is built around **hold points**. A hold point is an activity in its own right in
the programme: it takes time, it requires the Engineer's attendance, and work does
not proceed past it. There are **16 hold points** in the programme, and they are
placed at the moments where an error becomes permanent — the formation before it is
covered, the tanking before it is buried, the reinforcement before it is cast in,
the masonry before it is plastered.

**Inspection types.** `HOLD` — work stops until released. `WITNESS` — the Engineer
is invited and work may proceed if attendance is waived. `TEST` — a measurement
against a stated acceptance criterion. `SURVEILLANCE` — ongoing observation.

## The five checks that matter most on this project

**1. The formation (`Q-03`, hold point `H-01`).** The hazard is not the basalt, it
is the red-bole and vesicular seams at the flow contacts. A single seam under the
mat produces the differential-support case that sizes the mat. Every seam is
over-excavated and replaced with M15, and the approval carries a seam map.

**2. The tanking before it is covered (`Q-20`, hold points `H-02`, `H-09`,
`H-10`).** The external tank is continuous — under the mat, up the walls, over the
roof. Once it is backfilled it can never be seen again, and the structure sits with
its roof 2 m below grade and a design water table at the roof level.

**3. Reinforcement at 150 spacing both curtains (`Q-09` to `Q-11`).** The 150 mm
maximum bar spacing is an **EMP requirement** and is stricter than IS 456. It is not
a strength requirement, which means a site engineer looking only at strength will
see no reason not to relax it. It must not be relaxed.

**4. Formwork striking (`Q-16`, IS 456 Cl. 11.3 Table 11).** Props to a slab
spanning over 4.5 m stay for **14 days**. The pressure slab spans 5.000 m clear.
Striking requires a signed permit; the 14 days are in the baseline programme and
are not available for compression.

**5. Sentry post masonry line, level and plumb (`Q-25`, hold points `H-15`,
`H-16`).** Checked at the end of each storey, before plaster. Plumb over the 2.600
storey height and joint thickness are the two measurements that decide whether the
plaster can be held to its stated thickness — and once plaster is on, neither can
be corrected.

| Brick compressive strength | ≥ 10 N/mm² average | IS 3495 (Part 1) | Before order, and per delivery lot |

| Efflorescence | Within the IS 1077 limit | IS 3495 (Part 3) | Before order |
| Warpage | Within the IS 1077 limit | IS 3495 (Part 4) | Before order |
| Sampling | Sample size and selection | IS 5454 | Each lot |
| Soaking before laying | Bricks thoroughly wet, not surface-damp | IS 2212 | Continuous |
| Mortar proportioning | CM 1:6 by **gauge box**, not by shovel | IS 2250 | Each batch |
| Mortar working time | Used within 30 minutes; never re-tempered | IS 2250 | Each batch |
| Sand for mortar | Grading and cleanliness | IS 2116 | Source and each delivery |
| Bond | English bond, one brick thick | IS 2212 | Continuous |
| Joint thickness | 10 mm nominal, fully filled bed, cross and vertical | IS 2212 | Every course |
| Lift height | Not more than 1 m above adjacent work in a day | IS 2212 | Daily |
| Level | Every fourth course | IS 2212 | Continuous |
| Plumb | Over the full 2.600 storey height | IS 2212 | End of each storey — **hold point** |
| Frame interface | Top course wedged and packed only after initial shrinkage | IS 1905 | Before plaster — **hold point** |
| Wall ties to the columns | At the specified spacing — **detail does not yet exist** | — | Before plaster |

| Curing | Damp for at least 7 days | IS 2212 | After each storey |
| Chases for conduit | **Cut, not hammered**; not before the masonry has cured | IS 2212 | Electrical first fix |
| Plaster | Thickness, line, level, no hollowness on tapping, 7-day cure | IS 1661 | Each face |

## Non-conformance

A non-conformance is raised the moment it is identified, by anyone, and is closed
only by the QA/QC Engineer against evidence. Three categories of non-conformance on
this project are **not** closable by repair and require the designer's ruling:
reinforcement spacing relaxed beyond 150 in the protective envelope; a construction
joint formed without both waterstops and the EMP strap; and any penetration cut
through the envelope after casting.
